title: An accordion that animates to auto
description: interpolate-size and ::details-content let a details element transition to its natural height.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interpolate-size JavaScript that measures the content and animates a pixel height. `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` and `::details-content` transition a `<details>` to its natural height. details-content interpolate-size

title: Hover cards without JavaScript
description: interestfor, popover=hint and anchor positioning open a hover card on hover and focus.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback interestfor Timers for hover intent, focus and blur listeners, and a positioning library that measures and flips the card. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning places it. anchor-positioning interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Squircle avatars with corner-shape
description: aspect-ratio, :has(img) and corner-shape for avatars.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback corner-shape An SVG mask or a `clip-path` path: a fixed shape that clips borders and shadows too. `corner-shape: squircle` draws the corner, and `aspect-ratio: 1` keeps the avatar square. aspect-ratio corner-shape has

title: One Button, no IconButton
description: :has(> svg:only-child) turns any Button into an icon button.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback Gotchas :has() A separate `IconButton` component or an `iconOnly` prop, with every size and variant built twice. `:has(> svg:only-child)` lets the button see that it only holds an icon. has

title: Severity colors from one source color
description: Relative colors and light-dark() derive every severity shade from one color.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback oklch(from …) 40 hand-picked colors for five severities in two schemes, or a preprocessor that only works at build time. One `--ui-palette-source` per severity, and `oklch(from …)` derives every shade. light-dark relative-color

title: A carousel made of CSS
description: Scroll snap, ::scroll-button() and ::scroll-marker: a carousel without JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback ::scroll-button() JavaScript that listens to scroll events to run the buttons and dots, with their accessibility done by hand. `::scroll-button()` and `::scroll-marker` generate focusable buttons and dots. scroll-buttons scroll-markers scroll-snap

title: Drawing a checkbox
description: appearance: none, a clip-path checkmark and system colors for a native checkbox.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A hidden input and a fake box with an SVG check that mirrors every state. `appearance: none` lets the real input draw its own box and check. appearance clip-path

title: Leader lines with grid
description: A container query and a grid pseudo-element draw dotted leader lines.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @container A row of clipped dots, a repeating background or an empty filler element, and a media query that only knows the viewport. A grid per pair with a dotted `::after` between term and description, and a container query for the column. container-queries

title: Dialogs without JavaScript
description: Invoker commands, closedby and @starting-style for modal dialogs.
headings: The problem The trick Keyboard shortcuts Try it Scroll lock Fallback closedby A click handler for `showModal()`, another for `close()`, and a backdrop listener that checks where the click landed. `commandfor`, `command` and `closedby` open and close it, `@starting-style` fades it in, and `allow-discrete` fades it out. dialog-closedby invoker-commands overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Sliding drawers with @starting-style
description: A dialog that slides in from any edge, and out again with allow-discrete.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback @starting-style A fixed `<div>` with JavaScript for the focus trap, Esc and backdrop clicks, and a class removed after `transitionend` to animate it out. A modal `<dialog>` that slides with `translate`, `@starting-style` and `allow-discrete`. display-animation overlay starting-style transition-behavior

title: Fluid type with progress()
description: progress() turns the viewport width into one 0 to 1 ramp that the four fluid heading sizes share.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback progress() A clamp() per heading with a hand-tuned vi slope, so every heading grew over a different range of viewport widths. `progress(100vi, start, end)` is one shared ramp, and each fluid heading mixes its two steps with it. progress-function

title: Smarter fieldsets with :has()
description: :has() lets fieldsets and legends style themselves from what they contain.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :has(:required) Modifier classes or props kept in sync with what the fieldset contains. `:has()` lets the fieldset and legend style themselves from their content. has

title: Menus with popover and anchor positioning
description: Popover, invoker commands and anchor positioning: a menu with no JavaScript.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback popover JavaScript to toggle and dismiss it, `z-index` fights, and a positioning library that measures and flips. `popover`, invoker commands and anchor positioning, with the trigger as the implicit anchor. anchor-positioning invoker-commands popover

title: Styling the native progress bar
description: appearance: none and :indeterminate on the native progress element.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :indeterminate A `<div role="progressbar">` with its ARIA attributes kept in sync by hand. The native `<progress>` with `appearance: none`, so the role and the value stay native. appearance container-style-queries indeterminate

title: Range sliders with datalist ticks
description: A scroll-driven gradient fill and datalist tick marks for input range.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback <datalist> Vendor pseudo-elements, a fill only Firefox could draw, and tick labels that never showed. A scroll-driven animation on the thumb fills the track, and `display: flex` brings the `<datalist>` labels back. datalist input-range scroll-driven-animations

headings: It's a proper design system now Five example themes Token tiers Contrast as a guarantee Loads of new components So much cool stuff in the docs Blocks! Theme builder The CSS is the component One Astro file, five frameworks Slots become parts, props get one naming model The platform did the work Browser support, honestly The new "by hand" Working with AI Where it landed Migrating

title: A select you can style
description: appearance: base-select, ::picker(select) and :open for a fully styled select.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback base-select A rebuilt listbox: a button, a popup, ARIA roles and JavaScript for focus, keyboard and typeahead. `appearance: base-select` makes the real `<select>` stylable, with `<selectedcontent>` and `::picker(select)`. customizable-select open-pseudo

title: Spinners from aria-busy
description: aria-busy=true is all it takes to show a spinner.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback aria-busy A spinner class for sighted users and `aria-busy` for assistive technology, kept in sync. `[aria-busy="true"]` is the only switch, and a `::before` ring spins. animations-css not

title: A switch from a checkbox
description: A native checkbox, appearance: none and an outline trick.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback appearance: none A `<button>` with `aria-checked` toggled in JavaScript, or a hidden checkbox plus extra spans. `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` with `appearance: none` draws its own track and dot. appearance light-dark

title: A header that knows it's stuck
description: scroll-state() container queries give a stuck table header and a scrolled dialog their shadows.
headings: The problem The trick Scroll shadows Try it Fallback scroll-state() A scroll listener, or an `IntersectionObserver` with a sentinel element. `container-type: scroll-state` and `@container scroll-state(stuck: block-start)` show the shadow. anchor-positioning container-scroll-state-queries

title: Tabs from radio buttons
description: Radio inputs, a grid and :nth-child(of S) for CSS-only tabs.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :nth-child(of S) JavaScript for clicks, `aria-selected` and panels, or CSS tabs with one selector per tab. One radio group, and `:checked + label + panel` shows the right panel. nth-child-of sibling-count

title: Validation that waits with :user-invalid
description: :user-invalid shows errors after the user interacts, not on page load.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback :user-invalid JavaScript that adds a touched class on blur. `:user-invalid` only matches after the user has changed the field and left it, or tried to submit. user-pseudos

title: Textareas that grow with field-sizing
description: field-sizing: content and lh units for auto-growing textareas.
headings: The problem The trick Try it Fallback field-sizing JavaScript that resets the height to `scrollHeight` on every keystroke. `field-sizing: content` grows and shrinks the textarea with its text. field-sizing lh

title: Tooltips with interestfor
description: interestfor, calc-size() and @position-try for tooltips that stay on screen.
headings: The problem The trick Staying on screen Try it Fallback interestfor Event listeners, delays and a positioning library that measures and flips. `interestfor` and `popover="hint"` open it on hover and focus, and anchor positioning keeps it on screen. anchor-positioning calc-size interest-invokers popover-hint

title: Vertical rhythm with round()
description: round() snaps line heights and font sizes to a rhythm step.

api: AccordionSummary The always visible header. The marker. Renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. marker

title: Accordion API
description: Reference for Accordion Solid component.
api: Accordion Container element. The always visible header. The marker. In Astro, React, Solid, Svelte and Vue, `AccordionSummary` renders a chevron by default. Only `.ui-marker` animates. The collapsible content. A group of actions, such as buttons. name Groups accordions so only one of them can be open at a time. markerAnimation How the marker animates when the accordion opens. `rotate` turns it upside down, `flip` mirrors it, and `turn` turns it a quarter turn, for a marker that points to the inline end and then points down when open. The default chevron points down, so `turn` needs a custom marker. open Whether the accordion is open. variant The variant to use. The default `plain` accordion has the page surface and no border, like a Card. `transparent` has no surface or border, and no inline padding.

title: Anchor API
description: Reference for Anchor Solid component.
api: Anchor Container element. Scopes the anchor to its content. The content the floating content is anchored to. The floating content. With `trigger="hover"`, it takes the anchor's `id` and `popover="hint"` over its own, so the trigger's `interestfor` always reaches it. In an anchor that always shows it, its own `id` and `popover` stay. id The id of the root. With `trigger="hover"`, the id of `AnchorContent`. Add `interestfor` with the same id to the trigger. Required with `trigger="hover"`. positionArea Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the floating content is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the content's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page. trigger Shows the floating content on hover and focus with `popover="hint"`. Without it, the content always shows.

title: Avatar group API
description: Reference for Avatar group Solid component.
api: AvatarGroup A group of overlapping avatars. aria-label The accessible name of the group. The Astro, React, Solid and Svelte types require it, or `aria-labelledby`. In Vue it passes through as an attribute. aria-labelledby The id of the element that names the group, instead of `aria-label`. role The `role` of the root. A passed role replaces `group`.

title: Avatar API
description: Reference for Avatar Solid component.
api: Avatar Container element. The avatar image. Its `alt` is `label`. label src aria-label The accessible name of a link or button avatar, instead of `label`. The Astro, React, Solid and Svelte types require one of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` on a link or button. In Vue it passes through as an attribute. aria-labelledby The id of the element that names a link or button avatar, instead of `label`. as The element to render, or the link component of your router with `href`, such as Next's `Link`, Solid Router's `A` or Nuxt's `NuxtLink`, which gets the `href`. Defaults to `"a"` with `href`. With `disabled`, it renders a plain `<a>` with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` instead. disabled Disables a button avatar. A link avatar drops its `href` and gets `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` instead. href The link to use. Renders an `<a>`. label The name of the person or thing: the `alt` of the image, or visually hidden text next to the letters or icon. Leave it out when the name is shown next to the avatar, which then is decorative. A link or button avatar needs it. shape The shape of the avatar. size The size of the element. src The image source. Replaces the content. Without it, the avatar shows its content, so a missing photo falls back to the letters. variant The variant to use. `filled` is the primary color, `outlined` the border color with no fill and `tonal` the primary tint.

title: Badge API
description: Reference for Badge Solid component.
api: Badge Container element. The element the badge is anchored to. default The indicator, inside `.ui-floating`. Holds `label`, the visible text with `hideLabel`, or only screen reader text with `dot`. label indicator color Optional colors. corner The corner the indicator sits on. dot Renders the indicator as a dot. `label` stays as screen reader text, and the `indicator` slot isn't shown. hideLabel Hides `label` visually, for the whole sentence screen readers read, such as "5 unread messages". The `indicator` slot then holds the visible text and is hidden from screen readers. invisible Hides the indicator. label The indicator text, such as a count. With `hideLabel` or `dot`, only screen readers get it.

title: Button API
description: Reference for Button Solid component.
api: Button Container element. An optional icon. The label next to an icon. The CSS styles the `span`, and `.ui-text` is a hook for your own styles. An optional keyboard hint. aria-label The accessible name, for a button without visible text. React, Solid and Svelte require it, or `aria-labelledby`, when there are no `children`. aria-labelledby The id of the element that names a button without visible text, instead of `aria-label`. as The element to render, or the link component of your router with `href`, such as Next's `Link`, Solid Router's `A` or Nuxt's `NuxtLink`, which gets the `href`. Defaults to `"a"` with `href`. With `disabled`, it renders a plain `<a>` with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` instead. color Optional colors. disabled Disables the button. A link button drops its `href` and gets `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. href The link to use. Renders an `<a>`. round Fully rounded corners, a circle when icon-only. size The size of the element. type The button type. Use `"submit"` to submit a form, which a native `<button>` does by default. variant The variant to use.

title: Callout API
description: Reference for Callout Solid component.
api: Callout Container element, a `<div>`. With `closeButton`, the `<opui-callout>` custom element, which a button with `commandfor` and `command="--dismiss"` dismisses. An optional icon before the content. In Astro, React, Solid, Svelte and Vue, `CalloutIcon` renders the default one for critical, info, success and warning. The content, with an optional heading first. A close button, a `.ui-button` that is a direct child of the callout. It sits at the end of the first row. With `closeButton`, the component renders it with `command="--dismiss"` and `commandfor` naming the callout, hidden until `<opui-callout>` is defined. Renders a close icon by default, or the `svg` in `close-icon`. closeButton closeLabel close-icon A row of buttons under the content. closeButton Adds a close button at the end of the first row that hides the callout. The root becomes `<opui-callout>`, and the component loads `opui-css/elements/callout.js`, which runs the button. While the root has `data-hydrating`, which the React, Solid, Svelte and Vue components render until they hydrate, the button does nothing. closeLabel The accessible name of the close button. The types take it only with `closeButton`. id The id of the callout. With `closeButton`, the close button points at it with `commandfor`, so the component generates one when it's left out. onDismiss Called before the callout hides, with its cancelable `dismiss` event. `preventDefault()` keeps the callout, for example to ask first. severity The severity. Sets the color, and in Astro, React, Solid, Svelte and Vue the icon `CalloutIcon` renders. variant The variant to use. dismiss Fires on the callout before it hides. It bubbles, and `preventDefault()` keeps the callout. dismiss() Fires `dismiss` and, unless a listener cancels it, sets `hidden` on the callout and moves focus that was inside it to the next focusable element after it, or else the one before. Returns whether the callout hid.

title: Card header API
description: Reference for Card header Solid component.
api: CardHeader The card header. as The element to render. Use `div` for a header row with an avatar or a button next to the heading, and put the heading in an `hgroup` inside it. Use `header` for the same row in an `article` card.

title: Card API
description: Reference for Card Solid component.
api: Card Container element. An image or video that runs to the edges of the card. `img`, `picture` and `video` children fill the width and crop to the height you give them. The card header. The card content. A group of actions, such as buttons. as The element to render. Use `article` for a self-contained piece, like a blog post, a product or a comment, and `section` for a titled part of the page, like the settings of one feature. color Paints a thick `--ui-primary` outline around the card, for the one card in a row that stands out, like a recommended plan. density How much room the parts get. `spacious` pads them with `--ui-space-5` for a card that stands alone, such as a sign-in form, `dense` with `--ui-space-2` for a small stat. orientation The orientation of the element. With `auto`, a card whose first child is an image, picture or video puts it at the start, over the full height, with the other parts next to it, once the card is `40rem` wide, and on top below that. `horizontal` always puts it at the start and `vertical` always on top. The image takes `--_media-inline-size`, `40%` of the card. variant The variant to use. The default `plain` card has the page surface color and no border.

title: Carousel API
description: Reference for Carousel Solid component.
api: Carousel The scroller. The previous button. `::scroll-button(block-start)` when vertical. buttons previousLabel An item. default The next button. `::scroll-button(block-end)` when vertical. buttons nextLabel A marker, one per item. markerLabel markers align Where items snap. aria-label The accessible name of the carousel. The Astro, React, Solid and Svelte types require it, or `aria-labelledby`. title: Layout API
description: Reference for Layout Solid component.
api: Layout Any element. The classes only set its layout. align Where `.ui-layout-row` puts its children along the row, and where `.ui-layout-column` lines up its children and their text. bordered Draws a line in the middle of each gap of `.ui-layout-column`, `.ui-layout-row`, `.ui-layout-grid` and `.ui-layout-columns`, only between two children, so a wrapped row or the short last row of a grid starts and ends without one. Browsers without gap decorations leave the gap without the line. breakpoint The container width at which `.ui-layout-columns` goes from one column to `--_columns`: `40rem`, `56rem` or `72rem`. column A column with even space between its children. On a `ul` or `ol` it also drops the list bullets and margins. columns One column that becomes the `--_columns` tracks at the breakpoint, measured on the nearest container, such as `.ui-layout-container`. container Centers its content, caps its width and is the container `.ui-layout-columns` measures. grid Columns that fill the width and wrap. On a `ul` or `ol` it also drops the list bullets and margins, and a `.ui-card` in each `li` fills its cell. media A media object: a fixed-size start, such as an avatar, next to text that fills the rest and wraps instead of widening the row. row A wrapping row with its children centered vertically. On a `ul` or `ol` it also drops the list bullets and margins. gap The space between children of `.ui-layout-column`, `.ui-layout-row`, `.ui-layout-grid`, `.ui-layout-columns` and `.ui-layout-media`. spread Pushes the children of `.ui-layout-row` to its two ends, for a page header with a heading group and its actions. sticky On a child of `.ui-layout-columns`, keeps it in view at `--_sticky-inset` from the top while the other column scrolls, once the columns sit side by side. stretch Stretches the columns of `.ui-layout-grid` over the row when there are fewer children than fit, instead of leaving the rest empty.

title: List item API
description: Reference for List item Solid component.

The label, the first paragraph. label label Supporting text, the second paragraph. description description Optional content at the end, such as a value or an action. end Your own check, shown at the end while the row is selected or current. In a `Menu` or a listbox it replaces the default check. icon-checked as The element to render inside the `<li>`: `"a"`, `"button"` or the link component of your router with `href`, such as Next's `Link`, Solid Router's `A` or Nuxt's `NuxtLink`, which gets the `href`. A `<button>` gets `type="button"`, and a disabled link component renders a plain `<a>` with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` instead. borderTop Adds a border above the item. choice Wraps the content in a `<label>` for a checkbox, radio or switch. Can't be combined with `as` or `href`. color Optional colors. `critical` marks a destructive item in a [Menu](/components/menu). disabled Disables a button item. A link item drops its `href` and gets `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"` instead. for The `for` attribute of the `<label>` when `choice` is set. href The link to use. Use `ol` when the order is the content, like a ranking or steps. bordered Adds a border between list items. dense Packs the items tighter. flush Removes the inline padding of the items and the block padding of the list. role The `role` of the `<ul>`, such as `listbox`. `list` keeps Safari announcing a list. variant The variant to use.

title: Menu API
description: Reference for Menu Solid component.
api: Menu The menu surface, a popover anchored to its trigger. A group heading. HTML and CSS only. An item, holding a `<button>` or an `<a>` with `href`. Rendered from `items`, or a `ListItem` in the default slot. Optional content at the start, such as an icon. The label (`label` on an item). Optional content at the end, such as a shortcut in a `<kbd>` (`shortcut` on an item). Your own check on the current item, which replaces the default check. The `icon-checked` slot puts it on every item from `items`. icon-checked align Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. bordered Adds a border between the items. dense Packs the items tighter. id The id of the menu, which the trigger's `commandfor` points at. Required. items The items, as `{ as, borderTop, color, disabled, href, keepOpen, label, shortcut }` objects. `as` takes the link component of your router for a link item, such as Next's `Link`, Solid Router's `A` or Nuxt's `NuxtLink`, which gets the `href`. `borderTop` adds a border above the item, `color: "critical"` marks a destructive one, a disabled link has no `href`, also with `as`, and `keepOpen` keeps the menu open on click. Other keys go to the item's `<a>`, `<button>` or link component, like `type: "submit"` with `form` for an item that submits a form. orientation The orientation of the element. `horizontal` lays the items out in a row, for short labels such as emoji. popover The popover type. With `manual`, Esc and a click outside don't close the menu, and opening another menu doesn't either. side The side of the trigger the menu opens on.

title: Message API
description: Reference for Message Solid component.
api: Message A message. The sender's `Avatar`, from the `start` slot, shown on the last message of a run. It takes no `label`: `author` names the message. start The bubble. default The sender's name. author The time, and content such as a read receipt. datetime time Content after the time, such as a read receipt. end Buttons beside the bubble, such as a round `Button` that opens a horizontal `Menu` of emoji. On a device that can hover, they show while the message is hovered, holds focus or has a popover open. actions The `Reactions`, whose pills sit over the bottom edge of the bubble. bottom author The sender, shown on the first message of a run and read by screen readers on every message. datetime The machine-readable date and time of `time`. newAuthor Starts a new run when the author changes, for a group chat. outgoing A message you sent. It aligns to the end in the primary color, and its author is visually hidden. time The time as shown, at the end of the bubble. typing Shows animated dots instead of the content. The default slot becomes the status text for screen readers.

Point the input's `aria-describedby` at it. grouped Draws a dash between the two halves of the code. Add `spread` to put the input at the end, and `variant` to change the surface. disabled Dims the radio and shows a not-allowed cursor. `aria-disabled="true"` looks the same, but keeps the radio focusable and its value in the form, and doesn't stop the change, so block it with a script. error Marks the control invalid and shows error styles. hideLabel Visually hides the label, `.ui-sr-only` instead of `.ui-label`. id The id of the `<input>`. name The name of the `<input>`. Inside a `FieldGroup`, the group's `name` when omitted. orientation The orientation of the element. `vertical` stacks the label under the input. required The form won't submit until one radio in the group is checked. api: Rating A `<meter>` for a read-only score, or a `<fieldset>` of radios for input. The label of the input. label Clears the rating. title: Reactions API
description: Reference for Reactions Solid component.
api: Reactions The `<opui-reactions>` custom element, a row that wraps, and `display: contents` in the `bottom` slot of a `Message`. A click on a pill, or on a button with `command="--react"`, this element in `commandfor` and the emoji as its `value`, fires a `reaction` event that bubbles, and changes nothing. A pick of an emoji you already reacted with asks to uncheck it, and the menu the button is in closes. While it has `data-hydrating`, which the React, Solid, Svelte and Vue components render until they hydrate, clicks ask for nothing. The `ToggleGroup` of pills, named by the `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of the component. A reaction: a checkbox `ToggleButton` drawn as a pill, checked when you reacted with it. items quick The live region that `announce()` writes to, visually hidden with `.ui-sr-only`. aria-label The accessible name of the group of pills. The Astro, React, Solid and Svelte types require it, or `aria-labelledby`. In Vue it passes through as an attribute. aria-labelledby The id of the element that names the group of pills, instead of `aria-label`. items The reactions in use, as `{ aria-label, checked, label, value }` objects: the name with the count in `aria-label`, such as `Thumbs up, 2`, the emoji with the count in `label`, and `checked` on the ones you reacted with. name The `name` of the checkboxes. onReaction Called when a pill is clicked or an emoji is picked, with the emoji's `value` and the `checked` state asked for in `event.detail`. Nothing changes until you change `items`. quick The one-tap reaction, as an item without a count: `{ aria-label, label, value }`. Its pill always comes first. While `items` has no entry with its `value`, the pill is unchecked, has a dashed border and shows `label` alone. announce(message) Reads `message` to screen readers, through the `role="status"` child. delete(value) Removes the pill of `value`, and moves focus to the next pill, the previous one or the first button after the pills when the removed pill had it. The pill of the `quick-value` reaction stays, unchecked and `.ui-suggested`, with the `quick-label` and `quick-text` attributes as its name and text, and keeps focus. group The `.ui-toggle-group` of pills, or `null`. Read-only. reaction Fires when a pill is clicked, or a button with `command="--react"` and this element in `commandfor`, with the `value` and the `checked` state asked for in `event.detail`. It bubbles, and changes nothing. set(value, reaction) Updates the pill of `value` with `{ checked, label, text }`, the accessible name in `label` and the emoji and count in `text`, or adds one at the end, and the `quick-value` reaction first. It removes `.ui-suggested` from the pill.

title: Select all API
description: Reference for Select all Solid component.
api: SelectAll The `<opui-select-all>` custom element, `display: contents`, around the group, such as a `Fieldset` or a `Table`. The checkbox that checks and unchecks the other enabled checkboxes inside. It's checked when they all are, and `indeterminate` when some are. control The controlling checkbox, the one with `data-select-all`, or `null`. Read-only. items The enabled checkboxes it controls, in document order. Read-only. sync() Sets the controlling checkbox's `checked` and `indeterminate` from the others. The element calls it when one changes, so call it only after setting `checked` from a script.

title: Select button API
description: Reference for Select button Solid component.
api: SelectButton The select's button, showing the selected option in `<selectedcontent>`.

title: Sortable table API
description: Reference for Sortable table Solid component.
api: SortableTable The `<opui-sortable-table>` custom element, `display: contents`, around the table. It moves the body rows and announces the new order in its `role="status"` child, or one it adds. While it has `data-hydrating`, which the React, Solid, Svelte and Vue components render until they hydrate, header clicks do nothing. The button around a sortable header's label. A press sorts by its column, ascending first, and sets `aria-sort` on the header. ascendingLabel What a sort in ascending order announces, with `{column}` where the header's label goes. descendingLabel What a sort in descending order announces, with `{column}` where the header's label goes. onSort Called before the rows are sorted, with the column index, the direction and the header in `event.detail`. `preventDefault()` keeps the rows where they are. sort Fires before the rows move, with the column index, the direction and the header in `event.detail`. It bubbles, and `preventDefault()` keeps the rows where they are. sort(header, direction) Sorts by the column of `header`, in `direction` (`"ascending"` or `"descending"`), or else the other way from its `aria-sort`, ascending first. It fires `sort`, sets `aria-sort` and announces the order. table The `<table>` inside, or `null`. Read-only.

title: Spinner API
description: Reference for Spinner Solid component.
api: Spinner Renders a spinner pseudo-element on the element. Always indeterminate. size Spinner size follows the element's computed font size.

title: Stat API
description: Reference for Stat Solid component.
api: Stat A `dl` with the label, the value and the description, so a screen reader reads them as one term with its details. The label. label label The value, in tabular numbers. default The description. description description description Text under the value, such as the change since last week. label What the value counts, such as Visitors. size The size of the value.

title: Step button API
description: Reference for Step button Solid component.
api: StepButton A `.ui-button.ui-round` with `command="--step-down"` or `command="--step-up"`, showing a minus or a plus, or your icon. Disabled with the input, and `aria-disabled` at `min` or `max` or while the input is read-only or `aria-disabled`. Hidden until `<opui-step-button>` is defined. command Which way the button steps: `--step-down` or `--step-up`. for The `id` of the number input, as its button's `commandfor` and `aria-controls`. label The accessible name of the button, by `command`. Pass it translated. input The `<input>` its button's `commandfor` names, or `null`. Read-only. step() Steps the value by `step` in the button's direction, within `min` and `max` and unless the input is disabled or read-only, and fires `input` and `change`.

title: Stepper item API
description: Reference for Stepper item Solid component.
api: StepperItem A step. Replaces the check in the marker of a complete step. Hidden from screen readers. icon-complete The label, as a link back to the step. href label label A short line under the label. description description completeLabel Screen reader text after the label of a complete step. current Marks the current step. The steps before it show as complete, with or without `.ui-state-complete`. description A short line under the label. errorLabel Screen reader text after the label of a step with an error. href Renders the label as a link on a step with a `state`, but not on the current one. label The name of the step. state The step's state: `complete` shows a check in the marker and the line to the next step in the accent color, `error` an exclamation mark in the marker and the label in the invalid color. Without it the step is still to come, or the current one.

title: Stepper API
description: Reference for Stepper Solid component.
api: Stepper The list of steps. A step, with its marker and the line to the next one. current items aria-label Accessible name of the stepper. complete Marks every step in `items` complete. completeLabel Screen reader text after the label of a complete step in `items`. current The index of the current step in `items`, from 0. The steps before it are complete. errorLabel Screen reader text after the label of a step with an error in `items`. items The steps, as `{ completeLabel, current, description, errorLabel, href, label, state }` objects. A step's own `state` wins over the `complete` the stepper and `current` give it. orientation The orientation of the element. `auto` stacks the steps below `32rem`. size The size of the element.

title: Switch input API
description: Reference for Switch input Solid component.
api: SwitchInput The switch input, without a label. name The name of the `<input>`. Inside a `FieldGroup`, the group's `name` when omitted.

title: Switch API
description: Reference for Switch Solid component.
api: Switch Container element. The switch input. An optional icon on the track, shown while unchecked. icon-unchecked An optional icon on the track, shown while checked. icon-checked The label. label default Supporting text displayed below the label. endText end-text card Renders the switch as a card: a padded, outlined surface that tints when hovered and when checked, with the label and `endText` inside. Add `spread` to put the input at the end, and `variant` to change the surface. disabled Dims the switch and shows a not-allowed cursor. `aria-disabled="true"` looks the same, but keeps the switch focusable and its value in the form, and doesn't stop the change, so block it with a script. error Marks the control invalid and shows error styles. hideLabel Visually hides the label, `.ui-sr-only` instead of `.ui-label`. id The id of the `<input>`. name The name of the `<input>`. Inside a `FieldGroup`, the group's `name` when omitted. orientation The orientation of the element. `vertical` stacks the label under the switch. required Adds a required mark after the label. The form won't submit until it's on. size The size of the element. spread Pushes the label and the switch to opposite ends. value The value of the `<input>`, submitted with the form when it's checked. variant The surface of the card, with `card`. `outlined` has a border, `tonal` a tinted surface and `elevated` a shadow, like Card.

title: Table cell API
description: Reference for Table cell Solid component.
api: TableCell A data cell, inside `TableRow`. numeric Aligns the cell to the end and uses tabular figures, so the digits of a column line up.

title: Table column group API
description: Reference for Table column group Solid component.
api: TableColumnGroup A group of columns, before the table head.

title: Table column API
description: Reference for Table column Solid component.
api: TableColumn A column, inside `TableColumnGroup`. width The column width, merged into `style`.

title: Table header cell API
description: Reference for Table header cell Solid component.
api: TableHeaderCell A header cell, inside `TableRow`. numeric Aligns the header to the end, over a column of `numeric` cells. sortable Wraps the label in a `<button>` that sorts the table by this column, inside a `SortableTable`.

title: Table API
description: Reference for Table Solid component.
api: Table Container element. The header rows. A header cell. The body rows. A row. A data cell. Optional footer rows, such as totals. An optional title for the table. density The cell padding. flush Drops the block margin, for a table that sits in a card or another padded box. overflow What the table does when its columns don't fit. `wrap` lets the cells wrap their text, and `scroll` keeps each cell on one line, scrolls the table sideways and lets the last column take the space left over. Give a scrolling table `tabindex="0"`, so keyboard users can scroll it. stickyHeader Keeps the header rows at the top of the nearest scroll container. Offset it with `--_sticky-inset`.

title: Tabs item API
description: Reference for Tabs item Solid component.
api: TabsItem The radio input for a tab, followed by the tab and the panel. checked Selects the tab. id The id of the input. Generated when omitted. name Overrides the name shared by the tab inputs. value The value of the input. The tab is selected while it matches the `value` of `Tabs`.

title: Tabs label API
description: Reference for Tabs label Solid component.
api: TabsLabel The tab. for The id of the input it labels. Set by the item.

title: Tabs panel API
description: Reference for Tabs panel Solid component.
api: TabsPanel The panel.

title: Tabs API
description: Reference for Tabs Solid component.
api: Tabs Container element. A visually hidden radio input that holds a tab's state. The tab is its label. A tab. The panel of the selected tab. defaultValue The `value` of the tab selected at the start, when `value` is omitted. name The name shared by the tab inputs. Generated when omitted. onValueChange Called with the `value` of the tab when one is selected. orientation The orientation of the tabs. `vertical` stacks them in a column at the inline start, with the panel beside them. overflow What the tabs do when they don't fit. `scroll` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `wrap` wraps them onto more rows. Vertical tabs ignore it: long labels wrap within the column. role Makes tabs without panels a radio group, which `aria-label` names. Tabs with panels take no role: the root holds the panels, and a radio group holds only radios. variant The variant to use. The default `tonal` tabs sit on a tonal track and the selected tab is a raised pill. value The `value` of the selected tab. The item whose `value` matches is checked, and the items' own `checked` is ignored.

title: Textarea API
description: Reference for Textarea Solid component.
api: Textarea A `.ui-field` with a `<textarea>`. Your textarea, `rows` lines tall (3 by default), growing to `--_max-block-size` (20 lines). It resizes taller, and wider with `autoFit` (`.ui-auto-fit`).

title: Timeline item API
description: Reference for Timeline item Solid component.
api: TimelineItem An event. The date, in its own column. datetime time Replaces the dot with an icon. It follows the item's color and the current state. marker The title of the event. headingLevel label label color Optional colors. current Marks the current item, which fills its marker with `--ui-selected-strong` and a halo. `true` renders `aria-current="true"`, and `step`, `date` or `time` that value. datetime The machine-readable date of `time`. headingLevel The heading level of `label`, so the item fits the page outline. label The title of the event, rendered as a heading. time The date as shown, in the date column.

title: Timeline API
description: Reference for Timeline Solid component.
api: Timeline Container element. An event, with its marker and the line to the next one. items The items, as `{ color, current, datetime, description, headingLevel, label, time }` objects. `description` renders a paragraph. size The size of the element. tracked Colors the line and the plain markers before the current item with `--ui-selected-strong`, like a progress tracker.

title: Toast API
description: Reference for Toast Solid component.
api: Toaster The `<opui-toaster>` custom element, with `display: contents`. A button with `commandfor` and `command="--toast"` shows a toast with its `data-toast` text and `data-toast-severity`, and `toast(message, { action, duration, severity })` or `toast.success(message)` does it from a script, where `action` takes a `label` and an `onClick`, and `toaster` takes the id or the element of the toaster to show it in. The stack of toasts, a manual popover at the block end and the inline end of the viewport unless `side` and `align` move it. It opens with the first toast and closes after the last. A toast, a `Callout` with the severity class, its icon (an empty `svg` that `--_icon-image` masks), the message in `.ui-content`, an action `Button` when it has an `action`, and a close `Button`. The element adds it, and on dismiss makes it `inert`, fades it out and closes its gap before it removes it. The polite live region that announces each toast but a critical one, visually hidden with `.ui-sr-only` and outside the popover, so it's always in the page. The assertive live region that announces a critical toast at once, visually hidden like the status region. Without it, critical toasts go to the status region. align Where the toasts sit along their side of the viewport. closeLabel The accessible name of the close button of each toast. duration How long a toast stays, in milliseconds, while the pointer and focus are elsewhere. A toast with an action stays twice as long, and `Infinity` keeps a toast until it's closed. id The id the buttons point at with `commandfor`. Required. limit The most toasts shown at once. Past it, the oldest is dismissed, unless it holds focus. side The side of the viewport the toasts sit on. alert The `<div role="alert">` that announces critical toasts, or `null`. Read-only. dismiss(toast) Dismisses a toast: makes it `inert`, moves focus that was in it to the next toast, fades it out and removes it. Returns a promise that resolves once it's gone. list The `<ol>` that holds the toasts, or `null`. Read-only. show(message, options) Shows a toast and announces it, with the `action`, `duration` and `severity` options of `toast()`. Returns the toast's `<li>`, or `null` without a list. status The `<div role="status">` that announces the other toasts, or `null`. Read-only.

title: Toggle button API
description: Reference for Toggle button Solid component.
api: ToggleButton Container element. A visually hidden checkbox or radio input. checked Selects the button. disabled Dims the button and skips it with Tab and the arrow keys. `aria-disabled="true"` looks the same, but keeps the button focusable and its value in the form, and doesn't stop the change, so block it with a script. id The id of the `<input>`. label The button text when there is no child content. name The name of the input. Falls back to the `ToggleGroup`'s name, then to a `FieldGroup`'s. required The form won't submit until it's checked. A `ToggleGroup` without `multiple` needs it on one button only. size The size of the element. type The input type. `radio` allows one selection in a group. A `ToggleGroup` without `multiple` makes every button a radio. value The value of the input.

title: Toggle group API
description: Reference for Toggle group Solid component.
api: ToggleGroup Container element. A toggle button. defaultValue The starting selection when `value` is omitted. multiple Lets several buttons be checked, with checkbox inputs. Without it, one button is checked at a time, with radio inputs in a `[role="radiogroup"]`. name The name shared by the inputs. Generated when omitted. onValueChange Called with the new selection when a button is toggled. orientation The orientation of the element. overflow What the items do when they don't fit. `wrap` wraps them onto more rows, `scroll` keeps them on one row and scrolls it sideways, and `shrink` keeps them on one row and truncates labels with an ellipsis. Icon-only items keep their size. role The `role` of the root, such as `toolbar`. Without it, `radiogroup`, or `group` with `multiple`. size The size of the buttons. value The value of the checked button, or the values of the checked buttons with `multiple`. The buttons whose `value` matches are checked, and their own `checked` is ignored.

title: Tooltip API
description: Reference for Tooltip Solid component.
api: Tooltip Container element. The tooltip, a `popover="hint"`. The trigger that shows the tooltip on hover and focus. arrow Adds an arrow that points to the trigger. id The id of the tooltip. Add `interestfor` with the same id to the trigger, and on a toggletip `commandfor` and `command="toggle-popover"` too. Required. positionArea Any valid `position-area` value. Controls where the tooltip is placed. The `self-` keywords follow the tooltip's own direction, so the placement mirrors in a right-to-left part of a left-to-right page.

title: Typography API
description: Reference for Typography Solid component.
api: Typography Classless typography for uncontrolled child markup. blockquote Quoted block with a start border. caption Muted supporting text. codeBlock Monospace preformatted block. color Tone of `.ui-swatch`, and the text color of `.ui-p`, `.ui-caption` and `.ui-overline`. Without it, the swatch takes the palette accent of the scope it sits in. heading Heading styles for any element. headingGroup Groups an overline, heading, and optional body copy. icon Sizes an inline `svg` to `--ui-icon-size` and keeps it from shrinking in a flex row. inline Inline text element utilities. link Link styles outside `.ui-rich-text`. On hover and focus, the underline gets thicker. The color gets darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode. notRichText Ends the `.ui-rich-text` styles inside it. overline Small uppercase label text. paragraph Body paragraph styling. size Size modifiers on `.ui-p` and `.ui-icon`. An icon reads `--ui-icon-size-small` and `--ui-icon-size-large`. tabularNums Digits of one width, so numbers line up in a column of prices or stats. swatch A small colored dot for a legend, in `--_swatch-bg-color`, the palette accent of its tone or scope.
